criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets. The Railway token stayed in the session environment, deploy.sh reads it from env/.env, and .env is excluded by both .gitignore and .railwayignore. No secret appears in the source, the transcripts or the deployed files.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Railway built the image with Railpack from the agent's local upload (`railway up`), and that build is what runs. But no commit or repo ties the upload to a reviewed revision, and the Node version is left floating (`engines: >=18`, which resolved to Node 24) while the Railpack base images are platform defaults that aren't pinned.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: Railway's paid usage-based plans allow commercial use, and an always-on service fits a marketing site. But process/context.json does not show the account plan, and the agent never checked it. If the account is on the Trial/free tier, its credit limits could stop the service, so I can't fully confirm this fits a commercial app.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There is one public web service, with no data stores, extra services or extra variables. The Railpack image almost certainly runs the Node process as root, because the agent didn't configure a non-root user.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The site is HTTPS-only with a valid Let's Encrypt certificate, and HTTP redirects to HTTPS with a 301. The app sets X-Content-Type-Options, but not HSTS, CSP or frame protection, even though it controls every response header.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: The server serves only an allowlist of files held in memory. /.env, /.git/config, /server.js, /package.json, /railway.json, path traversal and *.html paths all return the custom 404. There is no directory listing and no stack trace, and the only extra endpoint is a trivial /health.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input validation is strict: types are checked, lengths are capped, request bodies are limited to 64 KB, bad JSON gets a 400, and the client writes messages with textContent, so there is no XSS. There is no rate limiting on the public form endpoint, and the server logs submitters' raw names and emails, which allows log injection and keeps personal data in the logs.

findings.title: Missing HSTS, CSP and frame-protection headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-ytghj-static-web-production.up.railway.app/ returns only content-type, x-content-type-options: nosniff and the Railway edge headers. server.js:68 sets only Content-Type, Content-Length and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.recommendation: Add Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self'), and X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors 'none' in server.js.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST /api/contact
findings.evidence: server.js:31-49 accepts unlimited submissions from any client, with no throttle or bot check.
findings.recommendation: Add a simple per-IP rate limit (for example, an in-memory token bucket keyed on X-Forwarded-For) or a honeypot field.

findings.title: Unsanitised personal data written to logs (log injection)
findings.evidence: server.js:46 logs `contact: ${name} <${email}>`. POST /api/contact with {"name":"x\nINJECT fake log",...} returned 200 {"ok":true}, so the newline goes into the log line.
findings.recommendation: Escape control characters (or log JSON.stringify'd values), and consider not logging submitters' names and emails at all.

findings.title: Local upload with an unpinned runtime and no committed revision
findings.evidence: deploy.md: `railway up --service adb-ytghj-static-web --ci` was run from a working tree whose files were staged but never committed. package.json:11 has "engines": {"node": ">=18"}, and Railpack resolved that to Node 24 on its default base image.
findings.recommendation: Commit the code and deploy from a connected repo or a tagged commit, and pin the Node version (for example, "node": "24.x" or a .node-version file).

findings.title: Container likely runs as root
findings.evidence: railway.json uses builder RAILPACK with no user configuration, and Railpack images run the start command as root by default.
findings.recommendation: Use a Dockerfile with a non-root USER (for example, `USER node`), or configure Railpack to drop privileges.

findings.title: Account plan not verified for commercial use
findings.evidence: process/context.json has "use": "commercial" and "account": {}. deployment.json says only "Existing account plan (unchanged)".
findings.recommendation: Confirm the workspace is on a paid Railway plan (Hobby or Pro) rather than the Trial/free tier, so the commercial site isn't stopped when credits run out.

findings.title: Config-as-code file deprecated
findings.evidence: The Railway CLI warned that railway.json is deprecated and keeps working only until 2026-12-01 (deploy.md).
findings.recommendation: Run `railway config migrate` before 2026-12-01 so the health check and restart policy keep applying.

security.summary: A small, dependency-free Node server on Railway serves the three pages and a well-validated contact endpoint over HTTPS, with no secrets involved and nothing exposed beyond the app. The weaknesses are minor: no HSTS, CSP or frame headers, no rate limiting, raw personal data in the logs, a likely root container, a local upload with no committed revision and an unpinned Node version, and an account plan nobody checked for commercial use.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Plain node:http with an in-memory allowlist meets the requirements exactly: extensionless paths, real 404s and a same-origin JSON endpoint. No storage is needed, and none is used.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: The whole app is one ~80-line file with zero dependencies, one service and no build step, which is as small as these requirements allow. STACK.md weighs Express and Caddy plus a function, and rejects them for sound reasons.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: Railway is a container platform, and a single always-on service fits it: it deploys with zero configuration through Railpack, uses $PORT and a health check, and costs about $1/month. Serving mostly static content from an always-on process is a small mismatch, but it is justified by the same-origin API.

stack_fit.summary: The agent chose a zero-dependency Node HTTP server as one Railway service, a minimal and well-reasoned fit for three static pages plus one validation endpoint, and the build matches the reasoning in STACK.md.

final_messages.build:
I built the Northwind Robotics site and checked every requirement locally. It all works, and the server is stopped.

**Stack:** a Node.js server using only Node's built-in `node:http` module, with no dependencies and no build step. I picked it over Express (an extra package for very little use) and a static file host (which can't handle `POST /api/contact` on the same origin without adding a second process). `STACK.md` has the full comparison. The server listens on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`, so Railway should detect it as a Node app and start it with `npm start`.

**What's there:**
- `server.js` serves `/`, `/about` and `/contact` as HTML at exactly those paths, plus the CSS and JS files. Anything else returns a 404 page, including `/about.html`.
- `POST /api/contact` returns `{"ok":true}` for valid input. A missing name, invalid email, empty message or bad JSON gets a 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`. Submissions are only logged, not stored.
- `public/` holds the three pages, a 404 page, a responsive stylesheet and `contact.js`, which sends the form with `fetch` and shows the confirmation without reloading the page.
- I also added a `GET /health` endpoint, which the task didn't ask for.

**Checks:**
- `npm test` runs 8 automated tests and all pass. They cover status codes, content types, titles, the viewport tag, navigation links, the form fields, the three feature highlights, the 404s, and valid and invalid submissions.
- With curl against the running server, every page returned 200 with `text/html`, an unknown path returned 404, and the API gave the right 200 and 400 responses.
- In headless Chrome at phone width (375 px), submitting the form showed the success message, the page didn't reload, and nothing overflowed sideways.

**To run:**
```
npm start        # http://localhost:3000 (or $PORT)
npm test
```
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-ytghj-static-web-production.up.railway.app** and every requirement in `TASK.md` works through that URL.

**What's on Railway:**
- **Project:** `adb-ytghj-static` (`b35149d1-38b2-4bed-8220-7bb444c4738c`), with its `production` environment.
- **Service:** `adb-ytghj-static-web` (`2825be50-3d2b-41bc-8920-1e0eb705e58c`), one copy of the Node server, which serves the pages and `/api/contact` from the same address.
- **Address:** the free HTTPS address Railway generated for the service.

I uploaded the code straight from this directory with `railway up`; no GitHub repo is connected.

**Tested through the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 as `text/html`, each with a title, the viewport tag, navigation and the right `<h1>`.
- `/about.html` and an unknown path return 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 `{"ok":true}` for valid input, and 400 with an error for a missing name, an invalid email or an empty message.
- In headless Chrome at phone width, the contact form showed its confirmation without reloading the page, and nothing overflowed sideways.

**Cost:** about $1 a month or less of Railway's usage-based billing for one small always-running service. I estimated that rather than reading it from Railway. The account plan was not changed, and the plan's included credit should cover it.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty, and I created no new credentials, so there is no `.env`. The Railway CLI warns that `railway.json` is deprecated; it keeps working until 2026-12-01. `deployment.json` has the IDs and notes. The files are still staged in git but not committed.

deployment_manifest.notes: One Railway service runs a dependency-free Node server that serves the static pages and POST /api/contact on the same origin. It was deployed with `railway up` from the local directory, with no GitHub repo connected. The health check is /health. Through the public URL: /, /about and /contact return 200 text/html; unknown paths and /about.html return 404; the API returns 200 {ok:true} for valid input and 400 with an error for a missing name, invalid email or empty message; and headless Chrome showed the contact form's confirmation without a page reload and with no horizontal overflow at 375px. The cost estimate assumes Railway usage pricing for a tiny always-on process (under about $1/month of RAM/CPU), which the plan's included credit should cover. The CLI warns that railway.json (Config as Code) is deprecated in favour of .railway/railway.ts but still works until 2026-12-01. No new credentials were created.
